methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
OSH Cut, a bootstrapped robotics and manufacturing company founded by Caleb and Jacom Chamberlain, lacks sufficient comparable transaction data for traditional valuation triangulation. The broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector comprises 11 public and private peers, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics at the private end, alongside one public comparable (277810.KQ). However, no subset of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers meets the minimum three-company threshold required for reliable peer-median analysis.

The peer-median method is inapplicable here due to insufficient narrow-set datapoints. A sector-wide median would risk material distortion given OSH Cut's early-stage, bootstrapped status versus the heterogeneous development phases and capital structures across the 11-company universe. Without transaction multiples, revenue multiples, or recent funding rounds tied directly to OSH Cut's operational profile, conventional public-market or late-stage private comps cannot be reliably extrapolated.

Valuation at this stage requires alternative approaches—founder equity stakes, cost-of-capital buildups, or future funding round expectations—rather than market multiples. The key uncertainty remains OSH Cut's addressable market traction and near-term capital needs, neither of which the current data set illuminates. A formal valuation range cannot be supported without additional operational metrics or comparable transaction evidence.
